met_analysis:
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Sri Ganganagar, Rohtak, Hamirpur, Sidhi, Ranchi, Digha and thence southeastwards towards Northwest Bay of Bengal and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Punjab & neighbourhood now lies over Haryana & neighbourhood and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over central parts of south Uttar Pradesh now lies over northeast Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood and extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Westcentral Bay of Bengal & adjoining north Coastal Andhra Pradesh between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough now runs from the above upper air cyclonic circulation over Westcentral Bay of Bengal & adjoining north Coastal Andhra Pradesh to Northeast Arabian sea across south Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, south Rajasthan and Gujarat between 3.1 & 5.8 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over north Chhattisgarh & neighbourhood and extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southward with height.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over North Jharkhand and adjoining Bihar extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The trough from the West Uttar Pradesh to North Gangetic West Bengal has merged with the Monsoon trough.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Central Assam & adjoining Nagaland between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
